info.title: Hanzo Cloud API
info.description: Package do is the org-scoped private-network surface — /v1/vpcs and /v1/balancers — carved out of Hanzo's OWN house DigitalOcean account.

get.summary: Returns every load balancer the caller's org owns, under the friendly names the org created them with.
get.description:
Returns every load balancer the caller's org owns, under the
friendly names the org created them with. Same account-wide filter as the VPC
listing: a load balancer outside the caller's "o"<orgHash>- namespace is never
in the answer.

post.summary: Creates a load balancer in the caller's org namespace and answers 201 with it.
post.description:
Creates a load balancer in the caller's org namespace and
answers 201 with it. The physical DigitalOcean name is derived server-side from
the validated org; a name that already exists there is a 409. Omitting
forwarding rules yields a usable HTTP 80→80 load balancer rather than a 422.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's load balancers and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's load balancers and answers
204. Ownership is confirmed by re-fetching the resource before anything is
deleted, so a cross-tenant id is a 404 rather than a delete of another org's
load balancer.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean resource id (a UUID), from the path.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's load balancers by id.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's load balancers by id. One that
exists in another org's namespace is reported 404, never 403 — the same
existence-oracle guard the VPC read applies.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean resource id (a UUID), from the path.

get.summary: Returns every VPC the caller's org owns, under the friendly names the org created them with.
get.description:
Returns every VPC the caller's org owns, under the friendly names the
org created them with. DigitalOcean is one account for the whole deployment, so
the account-wide inventory is filtered to the caller's own "o"<orgHash>- name
prefix and the prefix is stripped — another org's VPC is not merely hidden, it
is never in the answer.

post.summary: Creates a VPC in the caller's org namespace and answers 201 with it.
post.description:
Creates a VPC in the caller's org namespace and answers 201 with it.
The physical DigitalOcean name is derived server-side from the validated org,
so a tenant can only ever create inside its own namespace; a name that already
exists there is a 409.

delete.summary: Removes one of the caller org's VPCs and answers 204.
delete.description:
Removes one of the caller org's VPCs and answers 204. Ownership is
confirmed by re-fetching the resource and checking its physical name carries
the caller's org prefix BEFORE anything is deleted, so a cross-tenant id is a
404 rather than a delete of another org's VPC.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean resource id (a UUID), from the path.

get.summary: Returns one of the caller org's VPCs by id.
get.description:
Returns one of the caller org's VPCs by id. A VPC that exists but sits
in another org's namespace is reported 404, never 403 — the answer must not
tell one tenant that another tenant's resource exists.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: ID is the DigitalOcean resource id (a UUID), from the path.

forwarding_rules.description:
ForwardingRules are the listen→backend port mappings. Empty defaults to
plain HTTP 80→80, the same default DigitalOcean's own console applies.

name.description:
Name is the FRIENDLY name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40 characters. The
physical DigitalOcean name is derived from it and the caller's org.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug (nyc3, sfo3, …). Required.

size.description: Size is the DigitalOcean size slug. Empty takes DO's default.

type.description: Type is the DigitalOcean load-balancer type. Empty takes DO's default (REGIONAL).

ip_range.description: IPRange is the VPC's private CIDR. Empty lets DigitalOcean assign one.

name.description:
Name is the FRIENDLY name, a DNS-safe slug of at most 40 characters. The
physical DigitalOcean name is derived from it and the caller's org.

region.description: Region is the DigitalOcean region slug (nyc3, sfo3, …). Required.

entry_port.description: EntryPort is the port the load balancer listens on.

entry_protocol.description: EntryProtocol is the protocol the load balancer listens with (http, https, tcp).

target_port.description: TargetPort is the backend port traffic is forwarded to.

target_protocol.description: TargetProtocol is the protocol used to reach the backend droplets.

loadBalancers.description: LoadBalancers are the caller org's load balancers under their friendly names.

vpcs.description: VPCs are the caller org's VPCs under their friendly names.

bearer.description: The caller's credential, sent as `Authorization: Bearer <token>`. It is either an access token minted by Hanzo IAM or an API key (pk-/sk-). X-Authorization, and HTTP Basic carrying the token as the password, are accepted spellings of the same header for clients that cannot set Authorization; a browser presents the session cookie instead. Every operation requires it unless it says `security: []`.
